title: Illumina DNA Prep - BMS
author: Opentrons
materials: This protocol automates the [Illumina DNA prep protocol](https://support.illumina.com/content/dam/illumina-support/documents/documentation/chemistry_documentation/illumina_prep/illumina-dna-prep-reference-guide-1000000025416-09.pdf). Illumina DNA prep offers a fast, integrated workflow for a wide range of applications, from human whole-genome sequencing to amplicons, plasmids, and microbial species The protocol allows you to set the number of samples to 8, 16 or 24 (i.e. 8 samples per column, up to 3 columns). Samples are prepared in the wells by column (8 samples column 1, 16 samples columns 1 and 2, 24 samples columns 1, 2, and 3). See the [Illumina DNA Prep protocol](https://support.illumina.com/content/dam/illumina-support/documents/documentation/chemistry_documentation/illumina_prep/illumina-dna-prep-reference-guide-1000000025416-09.pdf) for more information about sample input requirements. Samples will end in columns 10 (for 8 samples), columns 10 and 11 (for 16 samples), and columns 10, 11, 12 (for 24 samples). The user can choose which steps of the protocol they want to run, or skip - see explanation of parameters below. **Plate Moving** The Protocol requires manually transferring the sample plate between the Thermocycler and Magnet 3 times. It starts on the Thermocycler and needs to be moved to the Magnet for the post-Tagmentation washes, and then moved to the Thermocycler for PCR and then back to the Magnet for the post-PCR cleanup. In the script the two positions are handled as sample_plate_mag and sample_plate_thermo; during calibration use an empty plate of the same labware as the sample plate on the magnet position to allow calibration. Explanation of parameters below: * `Number of samples`: 8 (column 1), 16 (column 1, 3), or 24 (column 1, 3, 5) samples (see above). * `Do a dry run?`: Sets the `Use modules?` parameter to `No` (see below). Tips will be returned, incubation steps skipped, and mixes shortened. This parameter is for testing purposes. * `Us
User seals the plate and the protocol incubates the samples with the mix in the thermocycler, 55 degrees for 15 minutes.
The thermocycler opens, and the user removes the seal.
The protocol performs two ethanol washes.

steps.title: Transfer plate between devices
steps.instruction: Manually move the sample plate as follows: start on the thermocycler, transfer to the magnet for post‑tagmentation washes, return to the thermocycler for PCR, then back to the magnet for post‑PCR cleanup. During calibration place an empty plate of the same labware on the magnet position.

substeps.instruction: Move plate from thermocycler to magnet (post‑tagmentation washes)
Move plate from magnet back to thermocycler (PCR)
Move plate from thermocycler to magnet again (post‑PCR cleanup)

steps.title: Set thermocycler block and lid temperatures
steps.instruction: Program the thermocycler block to 4 °C and set the lid temperature to 100 °C.

steps.title: Add tagmentation mix to samples
steps.instruction: Add the Illumina DNA Prep tagmentation mix to each sample well as specified by the kit.

steps.title: Seal plate and incubate at 55 °C
steps.instruction: Seal the plate securely and incubate in the thermocycler at 55 °C for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Remove thermocycler seal
steps.instruction: Open the thermocycler and remove the seal.

steps.title: Add tagmentation stop buffer
steps.instruction: Add the Tagmentation Stop Buffer to each well.

steps.title: Seal and incubate at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Reseal the plate and incubate at 37 °C for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Wash beads with tagmentation buffer
steps.instruction: Remove the seal, discard the supernatant, and wash the beads three times with Tagmentation Wash Buffer.

substeps.instruction: Wash beads – repeat 3 times with Tagmentation Wash Buffer

steps.title: Add PCR mix and barcodes
steps.instruction: Add PCR master mix and the appropriate barcoded adapters to each well.

steps.title: Run PCR and transfer supernatant
steps.instruction: Run the PCR program for 5 cycles (≈25 minutes). After PCR, transfer the supernatant to the output columns: column 7 for 8‑sample runs, columns 7 and 9 for 16‑sample runs, and columns 7, 9, 11 for 24‑sample runs.

steps.title: Post‑PCR cleanup with AMPure beads
steps.instruction: Perform post‑PCR cleanup by adding AMPure beads to the supernatant and following the bead‑based purification protocol.

steps.title: Perform two ethanol washes
steps.instruction: Wash the bead‑bound DNA twice with 80 % ethanol.

steps.title: Add resuspension buffer and collect final supernatant
steps.instruction: Add Resuspension Buffer (RSB) to the bead wells, mix, and transfer the cleared supernatant to the final output columns (8, 10, and 12) as appropriate for the number of samples.
